root_cause.text: ipc_idr_alloc() in the SysV IPC checkpoint/restore next_id path passed an unbounded upper limit to idr_alloc(), allowing allocation of IDR indices beyond ipc_mni even though SysV IPC IDs encode only the valid in-range index width, causing later lookup/removal to truncate to the wrong slot and leave stale entries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes idr_alloc(&ids->ipcs_idr, new, ipcid_to_idx(next_id), 0, GFP_NOWAIT) to use ipc_mni as the upper bound, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that the open-ended zero bound lets allocation spill past ipc_mni while new->id is still encoded as (new->seq << ipcmni_seq_shift()) + idx and later removed via ipcid_to_idx(ipcp->id), which truncates the real high IDR index and leaves a dangling IDR entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ipc_idr_alloc() to bound targeted ID allocation by ipc_mni so IPC IDs are allocated correctly within the valid range.
intent_record.what: The upper bound argument in the idr_alloc call inside ipc_idr_alloc() was changed from 0 to ipc_mni when allocating with a specific starting index derived from next_id.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the allocation is now constrained to the valid IPC identifier range up to ipc_mni instead of using 0 as the end bound, which would allow an invalid or unintended allocation range; this ensures IDs are allocated within the IPC maximum and makes the targeted allocation path work correctly.

grouping_result.intent: Fix ipc_idr_alloc() to bound targeted ID allocation by ipc_mni so IPC IDs are allocated correctly within the valid range.

That allows allocation of indices beyond ipc_mni, which is the root cause of incorrect IPC ID encoding and stale entries.
This is the upper-bound argument to idr_alloc(); using 0 means no effective limit, permitting allocation past ipc_mni. That directly embodies the bug described in the root cause.
